BlockContentKeywordsNote.message: This will applied to videos, comments, posts and playlists

CommaLineSeparationInfo.message:
In cases that the keyword must have a comma, insert a backslash (\) before the comma. Ex:
Bananas\, apples and oranges

CaseSensitiveInfo.message: When checked, words like "food" will not block content that includes "FOOD" or "FoOd"

ExactMatchInfo.message: When checked, the keyword must be the full name of the content. Example: "book" will not block "Facebook" or "book reading".

WordBoundaryInfo.message: When checked, it will only match if the keyword is a fully word. For example, "lever" will not block content that has "clever".

RemoveContentInfo.message: This will remove the blocked content from the page, instead of hiding behind a overlay.

GenericKeywordInfo.message:
Examples: 
"best" will match content like: "Best movie quotes" 
"top, hd" will match content like: "Top 10 albums of all time" and "Beautiful Landscapes (HD)"

With Regex:
"/a+/i" will match content like: "AaaaAAaAAAAaaAAA"
"/(official (music )?video)/i" will match content like: "Lorem Ipsum (Official Music Video)" and "(Official Video)"

Paragraph2API.message: API key has limits. In the free tier there's a maximum of 10.000 calls per day. The extension tries to minimize the number of call as much as possible, but it can still reach the quota if you navigate a lot in YouTube™.

APICacheInfo.message: API data received from videos will be reused for later when the video is found again. But the downside is that the data will not keep up-to-date with the video. Changes of title, description, tag, etc. will be ignored.
